title: Cost Efficiency of Large Infrastructure Projects
what_it_is: Cost Efficiency of Large Infrastructure Projects

sections.label: Scrutiny of large projects
sections.summary: Projects over $100 million, over two-thirds of infrastructure expenditure, are scrutinised by the overseeing Ministry and MOF before proceeding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Projects that exceed $100 million, which make up over two-thirds of our infrastructure expenditure, are subject to scrutiny by the Ministry overseeing the project as well as the Ministry of Finance (MOF) before they are allowed to proceed.

sections.label: Gateway Process for projects
sections.summary: A project estimated to cost above $500 million goes through a rigorous Gateway Process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If a project is estimated to cost above $500 million, it is put through a rigorous Gateway Process.

sections.label: Tuas Terminal material reuse
sections.summary: For Tuas Terminal Phase One, MPA reused excavated and dredged materials for land reclamation, saving a few hundred million dollars in sand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: One example is the construction of the Tuas Terminal Phase One where the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore came up with a method of reusing excavated and dredged materials from other sites for its land reclamation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This saved a few hundred million dollars by reducing the amount of sand needed.

sections.label: Re-approval for project changes
sections.summary: After approval, re-approval is required for material scope changes or cost increases exceeding 10% or $100 million, whichever is lower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: At any stage after a project is approved, re-approval is required if there are material changes to the project scope, or cost increases exceeding 10% or $100 million, whichever is lower.

sections.label: Funding options for mega projects
sections.summary: For mega projects, the optimal funding method is still being studied, with different ways not ruled out and no single model committed to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: My comments at this stage would simply be that when it comes to mega projects, we have to look at what is the most optimal way to do the funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are still in the process of doing that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We do not rule out different ways of doing the funding but we are not committed to a single model.

sections.label: Considering project lifetime cost
sections.summary: Project cost must consider not just initial development but cost over time, and how that should be dealt with and reflected is being examined.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Because our view is that when you look at the cost of a project, you must consider not just the initial development but how much that project is going to cost you over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, we are looking to see how that should be dealt with and reflected.
